Hi Lena / Tomoko —

Thanks again for the check-in last week. Per our renewal conversation, attached is a first-pass SOW and capacity table that reflects the key changes we discussed:

- Term: propose moving to a 24-month renewal (better unit economics for EU onshore nodes)
- EU residency: EU-primary ingestion + regional KV store (data-at-rest remains in EU by default)
- APAC: phased pilot (seed region in SG, warm-standby in tokyo) with clear canary windows before traffic cutover
- Cross-region failover: automated failover policy with 3-tier fallback (EU primary -> APAC warm-standby -> hosted fallback) and SLA targets listed in the SOW

Two immediate asks from our side: can you confirm desired pilot window (June or July), and whether your security team needs Customer-Managed Keys in EU KMS or Redwoods-managed KMS for the pilot?

I’ve attached: SOW_draft_EU-APAC.pdf and capacity_table_q2.csv (token throughput and expected burst patterns).

Propose a 30-min alignment call early next week to lock timelines and ownership (ops / security / procurement).

Thanks,

Hi Camila —

Thanks for the SOW and capacity file. A few clarifying items from security and procurement before we schedule the pilot:

1) KMS: For any EU-primary data we require customer-managed keys (our KMS). Can you confirm support and whether that adds any provisioning lead time?
2) Audit logs / retention: Compliance wants 12–24 months of immutable audit logs for inference requests (we currently log 18 months). What is Redwood’s default, and can we extend?
3) Cost model: The capacity table shows baseline tokens but not the committed vs burst pricing we discussed. Can you add a committed capacity tier for EU-primary nodes and a cost uplift for APAC warm-standby?
4) Canary: legal requested a short sample redline on the failover SLA (particularly around RTO/RPO and notification windows). We prefer the canary to be no longer than 48 hrs and with manual rollback controls.

We are generally aligned with the phased approach — June pilot is feasible if KMS provisioning can be done in the next 3 weeks. I’m available Tue/Wed next week for a call (CET).

Best,
Lena

Hi Lena —

Thanks for the quick review, and great questions. Quick answers inline below and I’ve attached an updated SOW with the security appendix we discussed.

1) KMS: We support customer-managed keys in EU (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault). There’s a 10–14 business-day provisioning window for KM export/validation on our side; we can start the paperwork immediately once you confirm the KMS account ID.

2) Audit logs / retention: Redwood defaults to 13 months of immutable audit logs for hosted + dedicated plans. We can extend to 24 months at an incremental storage cost — I’ve added the retention options to the SOW appendix (see updated_SOW_EU-APAC.pdf).

3) Cost model: I added committed-capacity tiers for EU-primary nodes in tab "CommittedTiers" inside schedule_apac_pilot.xlsx and a 15% uplift model for APAC warm-standby. If you prefer, we can present three committed-tier options on the call.

4) Canary: We can limit the canary to 48 hrs and expose manual rollback controls. The sample SLA redline is in the Drive link below (legal-friendly language).

Proposed timeline (high-level):
- Week of 3 June: EU KMS provisioning + acceptance tests (customer tech lead + Redwood infra)
- 17 June: APAC seed region activation (limited traffic)
- June–Aug: Canary cycles, ops runbooks, service-level verification
- September: Failover readiness sign-off (Ops + Security)

Call slots: Tue 14:00–15:00 CET or Wed 09:00–10:00 CET. Let me know which works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Links: https://drive.redwood.com/s/8a7SAm/updated-sow (SLA redline in appendix)

Thanks,
Camila

Attachments: updated_SOW_EU-APAC.pdf, schedule_apac_pilot.xlsx
